title: Irritable Bowel Syndrome: Dietary and Medical Management Ladder

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult IBS explanation, diet, lifestyle, symptom-led medicine classes and referral for refractory symptoms.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national irritable bowel syndrome guideline was identified in the sources opened on 14 October 2026. NICE guidance is an international comparator pending Saudi/local adaptation.
SFDA product registration was not verified; any medicine selection requires the current Saudi Drug Information register and hospital formulary.
NICE CG61 does not provide complete product-level doses, maximums or renal/hepatic adjustments for every IBS medicine.

pathophysiology.summary: Visceral hypersensitivity amplifies pain from normal gut activity. Altered motility contributes to diarrhoea or constipation. Dietary triggers vary between individuals. Psychological stress can amplify gut-brain symptoms without making them imaginary.
keyMechanisms: Visceral hypersensitivity amplifies pain from normal gut activity.
Altered motility contributes to diarrhoea or constipation.
Psychological stress can amplify gut-brain symptoms without making them imaginary.

symptoms: Pain, bloating, urgency, diarrhoea, constipation or mixed bowel habit.
physicalSigns: Abdominal tenderness may occur; reassess for new mass, weight loss, bleeding or dehydration.
redFlags: New bleeding, weight loss, anaemia, mass, fever, nocturnal progression or severe dehydration requires reassessment.
precipitants: Irregular meals, caffeine, alcohol, fizzy drinks, resistant starch, stress and individual foods.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Positive serology, bleeding, weight loss or objective inflammation.

clinicalManagement.title: Education, meals and activity
clinicalManagement.timeframe: First-line for at least one planned review cycle
actions: Use regular meals, adequate fluid, activity and individual reduction of caffeine, alcohol, fizzy drinks and resistant starch.
For diarrhoea avoid sorbitol; for wind/bloating trial oats or linseeds; adjust fibre toward soluble rather than insoluble sources.

clinicalManagement.title: Dietitian-led restriction when needed
actions: Refer for a structured single-food or low-FODMAP exclusion and reintroduction programme delivered by a clinician with dietary expertise.
Avoid long-term unsupervised restriction and monitor weight and nutritional adequacy.

clinicalManagement.title: Use symptom-led medicines through the local formulary
actions: Select an antispasmodic, laxative or antidiarrhoeal class according to the dominant symptom and stool consistency.
If symptoms persist, specialist-supervised neuromodulator or psychological therapy may be appropriate.
Stop ineffective treatment and reassess alarm features before escalation.

medicationPlan.note: NICE CG61 recommends medicine classes and dose titration but the opened guidance does not provide complete dose, route, frequency, duration, maximum and organ-adjustment details for every product. Use current SFDA product information and the Saudi/local formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Use only when symptoms persist despite general dietary and lifestyle advice.

teaching.scope: Adult IBS explanation, diet, lifestyle, symptom-led medicine classes and referral for refractory symptoms.
learningObjectives: Build a staged diet and symptom-management plan.
pitfalls: Escalating treatment without rechecking alarm features.
keyPoints: Match treatment to the dominant symptom.
Dietary exclusion needs planned reintroduction and nutritional oversight.

patientEducation: Set realistic goals around function and symptom reduction rather than a guaranteed cure.
lifestyleAndDiet: Regular meals, hydration, activity and individual trigger reduction.
mdtReferrals: Primary care, gastroenterology, specialist dietitian and psychological therapy service when indicated.
dischargeCriteria: Symptoms acceptably controlled, nutrition safe, alarm features absent and self-management plan understood.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review benefit and adverse effects after each intervention; reopen diagnosis if the pattern changes.
